searchText: b"h phase two critique — thirty additional improvements 1. use immutable tunnel routing. 2. recover durable receipts after disconnects. 3. avoid duplicate command dispatch. 4. keep one spawning action at a time. 5. allow active agents only on disjoint scopes. 6. require structured agent receipts. 7. verify every agent claim independently. 8. pin the original worktree before edits. 9. distinguish generated from authored files. 10. preserve public exports. 11. check all call sites before rewrites. 12. detect circular imports. 13. test deterministic clocks. 14. compare preview/export frame hashes where possible. 15. confirm title card safe areas. 16. confirm captions survive camera cuts. 17. confirm eyes remain legible at 180×300. 18. confirm fingers do not alias into noise. 19. confirm heel/toe silhouettes. 20. confirm garments do not merge with limbs. 21. confirm crossed arms remain locked. 22. confirm pocket hands remain locked. 23. confirm viseme changes span spoken intervals. 24. confirm blinks are deterministic. 25. confirm gaze is view space aware. 26. confirm startup restore from a clean process. 27. confirm packaged media is self contained. 28. record file sizes and sha 256 hashes. 29. inspect representative pixels directly. 30. keep next action executable until all evidence closes.

searchText: b"h phase three — final brainstorm the final method combines skeptical archaeology, sequential delegation, whole file repair, and proof courts. the awtsmoos is beyond every vessel yet renews each vessel now; therefore no cached belief is accepted as present truth. every feature is followed from authored state into geometry and pixels. every success creates a shadow audit. every export is opened, measured, hashed, and compared with its source project. every browser proof must show the loaded production canvas, not a shell. the system is considered complete only when independent auditors fail to find a meaningful defect and the master verification, render, persistence, export, pixel, and compliance gates all pass on the current tree.
